title: bring a document back in line with the code
display: docs back in line with the code
about: One narrow job written out: a document claims things the code no longer does, and this is the shape of putting that right. It is here as a worked example of what a template IS — steps of your own, plus `merge` named from the library so its review comes along — and not as the shape a job takes. Most jobs look nothing like this one. Take it when the job is this job, and write your own steps when it is not. The `after` on each step is its place in the order: entry numbers, 1-based, and what the board draws the arrows from. It is also a worked example of the FIELDS a step carries, so the copy arrives with one example of each already filled in — a checkpoint on the first step, an owner and an output on the second, a second try and the note explaining it on the third, a skip and its reason on the fourth, and a gate on the merge. They are examples and not your job: overwrite each with what is true, or empty it, before the plan is a plan. `sb plugin plans guide` says who writes which of them and when.

steps.name: list every claim the document makes about the code
check each claim against the code; write down which have drifted and how
steps.owner: <the agent you hand this step to>
steps.output:
Claims checked

- 11 claims, 3 of them drifted.
  - Two name a verb that was removed; one describes an order the code no longer keeps.
- Nothing here is a code change: the document moves, the code does not.

steps.name: rewrite what drifted, and cut what the code no longer does at all
notes: First pass rewrote a section describing a verb the code had dropped entirely; redone as a cut.

steps.name: run every example and command the document gives
steps.why: the document gives no runnable examples — there is nothing here to run.

steps.gate: Andrew reads the rewritten sections and says they say what he meant.

notes: Copied from the `docs` template. Add, drop and reshape steps as the job turns out — nothing links this plan back to what it came from.

The optional fields arrived as EXAMPLES of what each one is for: the checkpoint, owner, output, second try, skip and gate in here describe the template's own worked job and not yours. Replace or empty each one before working the plan.
